title: lease-handoff-burst-ledger-snapshot-mismatch-causing-prolonged-429s-across-hosted-dedicated-private
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Several customers experienced sustained 429s for ~45-90 minutes after an orchestrator leadership change. Root cause is a mismatch between the leader snapshot writer and the proxies' in-memory burst ledger reconciliation: during leader handoff the snapshot writer truncated recent burst-lease updates, causing restored ledgers to appear as 'fully exhausted' to proxies until the next refill window. This affected Hosted (routing fallback increased latencies and token exhaustion), Dedicated pools (local orchestrators returned hard 429s), and Private deployments that relied on the same snapshot protocol.

Impact: Intermittent but sustained request rejections for affected tenants, elevated error rates in 4 regions, multiple enterprise customers escalated to SE/CS.

Why this is unique: Unlike previous 'epoch jump' incidents, this was a snapshot serialization window where recent in-memory lease deltas were not included in the persisted snapshot because the handoff paused the delta applier. Proxies treated the restored state as definitive and applied strict enforcement without a grace reconciliation period.

Desired outcome: Implement snapshot-safe lease handoff, add a reconciliation grace window on proxy reconnect, and harden tests so leadership transitions cannot cause token-bucket regressions.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Incident reported by SE: sustained 429s for tenant 'acct-omega' in eu-west-1. Initial triage pointed to burst exhaustion on orchestrator X.

2026-03-10 09:45 - On-call (Dmitri): identified correlation with a leader election in the quota-orch service spanning 09:30-09:35. Observed snapshot files for several tenants were older-than-expected (missing recent 'burst-grant' deltas).

2026-03-10 10:10 - Mitigation applied: enabled proxy-side temporary-grace mode (30s) which accepts recent grants from peers for tenants with recent leadership change. Immediate 429 rate dropped by ~80%. Mitigation link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8321

2026-03-10 11:00 - Hotfix rolled to dedicated clusters: changed snapshot handler to flush pending burst deltas before finalizing handoff. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8332 (rollout job: ci/rollout-dedicated-2026-03-10).
2026-03-10 13:20 - Private customers: coordinated manual restart + snapshot patch with Customer Success for two impacted on-prem customers; both recovered after restart and snapshot rebuild.

2026-03-11 08:00 - Postmortem initial notes: root cause is a race where delta-applier goroutine can be paused by leadership checkpointing, causing last-window grants to be omitted. Proxy enforcement has been too strict: it immediately enforces restored counters without attempting short reconnect reconciliation.

2026-03-11 14:30 - Design discussion (with PM & SRE): agreed on three changes: 1) require snapshot pre-flush of pending burst deltas, 2) add proxy reconnect reconciliation window (default 60s) during which proxies accept 'soft' increase RPCs and don't convert to hard 429 until ledger fully stabilizes, 3) add leader-change e2e tests in CI simulating deltas-in-flight.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Code review feedback on PR 8332: add metrics for "snapshot_delta_gap" and ensure metrics emitted with tenant tag; SRE requests dashboards update: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/quotas/leadership-transitions
2026-03-12 17:40 - Canaries: rolled runtime-1.20 patched snapshot writer to 10% of hosted traffic and one dedicated pool. No regression observed for 36 hours in canary.
2026-03-13 10:05 - Follow-up: adding automated chaos test to leadership-change suite to inject snapshot pauses and validate no more-than-5s enforcement drift. Ticket to add test: ENG-125642.
2026-03-13 12:15 - Communications: CS drafted customer notification and remediation steps; legal and trust reviewed language for impacted enterprise customers (thread: #cust-esc-os).
